fields.latestPosition: VWG - Low priority to fix up Modbus - requires shut to implement as well
fields.why:
Currently PLC logic has to cycle through each of the clients to get the health status. Currently it checks each client for a second before moving on. With some of these Prosoft modules having 11 Modbus clients, a device could go on for 10 seconds without realizing there is a communications loss. Similarly if communications is back to healthy again, it will need to wait up to 10 seconds to confirm that it is healthy again
[Image in form – see source document] (221-PLC-011 Modbus client status logic)
fields.design:
Update Prosoft configurations to map through the client status/error through to spare addressing in the Modbus map.
This will allow the health status of the Modbus connection to be monitored at all times for live health status.
[Image in form – see source document] (Prosoft MNet Client 11 config – populate Error/Status Pointer with spare memory allocation)

Replace Modbus health statuses where appropriate and generate alarm if Modbus is not healthy. Priority to be dependent on device – monitoring devices only should be low priority, devices used for control should be high priority. Note ensure adequate timeouts are in place (typically 2 seconds).

Create SCADA page to display Modbus statistics and data. Faceplate to be accessible from PLC page and show the following data:
- Total number of requests
- Total number of responses
- Total number of errors
- Configuration error word
- Current Error
- Last Error
fields.impact: CROs will see Modbus comms alarms prioritised by device criticality, plus a new Modbus diagnostics faceplate.
fields.scheduleNote: Low priority; requires a shutdown to implement (VWG).
